messages:
elana: Quick design check: we need clear semantics for pin TTLs when we use epoched pins. Right now TTL is attached to the active pin, but epochs can reapply pins post-expiry. Do we want TTL to be absolute wall-clock or relative to epoch application?
pete: I think TTL should be relative to the pin instance (i.e., starts when that pin is applied). If a new epoch re-pins, it gets a fresh TTL. Absolute expiry is confusing for rollouts that replay.
elana: ok that matches my intuition. Also thinking we should add `pin_epoch` (monotonic int) and `applied_at` ISO string to the pin record so historical rollouts can reconstruct timeline without touching model history.
sam: SGTM. For storage: keep pin_epoch and applied_at in the compact pin object. Keep provenance chain in model_history only. Add a `snapshot_truncated` flag if chain > 1.
pete: Edge case: what about manual overrides that want to keep pin beyond default TTL? We should include `override_by` and `override_reason` optional fields on the pin instance (nullable strings).
elana: Good idea. API contract: rollout snapshot includes the compact pin instance (fields: model_id, pin_epoch, applied_at, ttl_seconds, intent, override_by, override_reason, fingerprint, snapshot_truncated). All strings or numbers converted to strings in transport.
sam: Migration: backfill recent 120 days with best-effort applied_at from timeline; older rollouts get `applied_at: unknown` and `backfilled: true/false` flags.
pete: Clients must treat snapshot as immutable record for that rollout. Live model metadata is the current state. Document clearly.
ops-bot: ticket INFRA-3150 created for epoched-pin snapshot implementation and DATA-789 for backfill jobs.
elana: Action items: 1) add pin_epoch + applied_at to compact schema (pete) 2) add override fields and truncation flag (sam) 3) draft migration window and backfill plan (elana)
pete: I'll start the schema PR and include examples in API docs.
sam: I'll own the backfill spec and add telemetry for override usage.
elana: No objections, marking this as agreed and will file a short follow-up RFC note. :white_check_mark:
